video.description:
Learn to explain how SwiftUI animates your own values and keyframes: Animatable, animatableData & KeyframeAnimator, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Animatable - A protocol that lets a type tell SwiftUI which values can change step by step.
animatableData - The property that holds the values SwiftUI changes during an animation.
KeyframeAnimator - A view that moves a value through a list of steps, such as grow, spin and fade.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Animatable, animatableData and KeyframeAnimator in English?

dialogue.title: A smooth dial

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my custom dial jumps to the new angle. I want it to move smoothly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Make the type conform to Animatable. Then SwiftUI knows what to animate.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How does an Animatable type tell SwiftUI the values?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With animatableData. It holds the numbers that change during the animation.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, the getter returns `angle`, and the setter updates it at every step.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I returned a constant first, so nothing moved.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, animatableData must connect to the real value.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I animate many steps, like grow, spin and fade?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A start value and keyframes. It moves the value through each keyframe in order.
Make your dial Animatable so it turns smoothly.
